title: Python: D2 binding-enumeration holes: nonlocal two levels down, global in a class body, match capture
description: Reported by the Opus review of #150 (not yet probed): (1) a nonlocal declared two levels down is credited to the nearest enclosing function rather than the one that binds the name (applyScopeRedirects); (2) a global inside a class body is never moved to the module scope; (3) a match capture pattern (case x:) records no binding in the walker (parser node shape to be confirmed). Each makes a name look singly bound when it is not, which E1, N3 and every later single-binding rule rely on. Probe first, then red-before fixtures per hole, fix, mutation checks, per-site re-measure of the five pins.
implementationNotes: Built (DEC-303 (a31) item 3, D2). PROBE FIRST: tree-sitter-python (the grammar in use) parses a match capture as case_clause > case_pattern > dotted_name > identifier (ONE identifier is a capture, a dotted name is a value pattern), a star or ** capture as splat_pattern > identifier, an 'as' alias as a DIRECT identifier child of as_pattern (no as_pattern_target, so the existing addAsPatternBinding missed it), a class pattern's first child is the class and a keyword_pattern's first child the keyword (neither a binding), the value of a keyword pattern is a bare dotted_name child; a bare _ is an empty case_pattern and *_ an empty splat_pattern. So the hole was real for all three. (3) addMatchCaptures, run from the case_clause arm of the walker dispatch, records a rebound binding for each capture, in the enclosing scope. (2) applyScopeRedirects no longer skips class scopes: a global in a class body moves its binding to the module, and a nonlocal in a class body to the enclosing function (the second goes slightly beyond the task text, which names global; both are the same Python rule). (1) nonlocal target: the nearest enclosing function that HAS a binding of the name, not the nearest function; a function that only declares it nonlocal too holds no binding until the deeper one is moved in, and its own redirect carries it on (processing is deepest first), so no extra guard on global or nonlocal names is needed; with no binding found anywhere it falls back to the nearest function as before. D1 interplay: the D1 fixture 'global then assign' was a disclosed over-inclusion and is now a positive (the assignment goes to the module, the class keeps no binding, the lookup reaches the base). Fixtures (test/python-calls.test.ts 'D2'): (1) nonlocal rebind, augment and for two levels down refused, twins (inner never rebinds, binds another name), mid declaring nonlocal too, one level down, mid binding its own x; (2) global then assign and global then for in a class body refused, twins (another name, no global), nonlocal in a class body refused with its twin; (3) 11 capture shapes (plain, after a literal, star, sequence element, tuple, class keyword value, class positional, dict value, dict rest, as alias, nested as) x module and function scope refused, and 10 twins (wildcard, another name, K.x, x.K, x() class pattern, P(x=1), literal, *_, unrelated alias, plus a bare _ and *_ with _ bound earlier). RED BEFORE: against the dev source the 4 new or changed tests fail (nonlocal, class-body global, match capture, and the D1 global test); green after. Mutation checks (source restored, 11 mutants, each red): class redirect off 2, nearest-function 1, binds-any 1, dotted capture off 1, single-identifier test off 1, splat off 1, as alias off 1, as-alias... class name bound as capture 1, case_clause dispatch off 1; two underscore guards, a mutant on the global and nonlocal name tests in the nonlocal target, and the dotted underscore check survived mutation because they are equivalent (a bare _ and *_ never reach a binding; the cascade makes the declare-nonlocal test redundant) so they were removed. PER-SITE MEASURE, instrumented origin/dev 1ea5328 vs the branch, five pins, multiset diff, entry counts equal: ZERO changed sites on flask, jinja, httpx, rich, tqdm (bins identical), so no in-repo edge is created or removed and no bin moves on the pins. NOT MEASURED: precision; PEP 695 type aliases and with-as tuple targets are GCLI-107, not here. Gates: typecheck, lint, format:check, bun test 825 pass, lore check --strict 0.14.1.

CORRECTION to the build note above (same push): the mutation list there is garbled. The final run had 9 mutants, each red: class redirect off (2 red), nearest-function target, binds-any target, dotted capture off, single-identifier test off, splat off, as-alias off, class name bound as a capture, case_clause dispatch off (1 red each). Not 11. The guards removed as equivalent (survivors) were: the underscore checks in the splat, as-alias and dotted-name cases (a bare _ and *_ parse empty), and the global/nonlocal-name tests inside the nonlocal target search (the deepest-first cascade makes them redundant).
